summary: 14-day analysis of Nightscout telemetry and active AAPS closed-loop profile reveals strong overall glycaemic control (86.0% Time in Range, average 121.6 mg/dL), but elevated hypoglycemia risk (5.1% Time Below Range <70 mg/dL). Hypoglycemia is concentrated overnight (up to 18.5% TBR at 01:00) and in the early evening (15.3% TBR at 19:00). Zero carbohydrates are logged in telemetry, meaning the user relies entirely on Unannounced Meal (UAM) Super Micro Boluses (SMB). Excessive safety limits (Max IOB 25 U vs 19.7 U/day TDD, Max Basal 12 U/h) and hyper-reactive Dynamic ISF (70% adjustment factor) allow AAPS to over-deliver insulin during unannounced meal spikes, driving severe postprandial crashes.

analysis_steps.findings: Sensor coverage is excellent at 98.7% with minimal gaps across the 14-day window. Profile configuration is authoritative and active. Zero carb treatments are logged in Nightscout across the entire period.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid glucose readings out of 4,046 expected; 10 minor gaps (largest 65 min); total carbs logged = 0.0g across 2,315 treatment entries.
data_gaps: Complete absence of carb treatment logs prevents direct empirical evaluation of Carb Ratios (CR) independent of loop UAM heuristics.

analysis_steps.findings: Primary safety concern is Time Below Range of 5.1% (<70 mg/dL), exceeding the clinical safety ceiling of 4.0%. Glycemic variability is elevated (CV = 32.6%). Severe low extremes reach 41 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: TBR 5.1% (<70 mg/dL) with severe low spikes down to 41 mg/dL on Aug 14 at 18:09 UTC and 42 mg/dL on Aug 13 at 17:09 UTC and Aug 21 at 06:19 UTC.
data_gaps: Unlogged meal timing obscures whether late afternoon lows are driven by UAM over-bolusing, physical activity, or basal excess.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight glucose experiences severe recurrent hypoglycemia (TBR 18.5% at 01:00, 11.4% at 00:00). Overnight target of 90 mg/dL from 00:00-08:00 provides zero safety buffer against overnight lows.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local glucose shows TBR at 00:00 is 11.4%, 01:00 is 18.5%, 02:00 is 10.1%, and 03:00 is 10.2%. Target profile segment at 00:00 is set to 90 mg/dL.
data_gaps: Lack of structured fasting tests makes it necessary to separate basal effects from residual evening meal insulin tails.

analysis_steps.findings: Static baseline ISF is 56 mg/dL/U with a 10-hour DIA. However, active Dynamic ISF significantly tightens effective ISF during high glucose readings, driving rapid insulin accumulation.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile ISF segment is flat 56 mg/dL/U. Dynamic sensitivity enabled with 70% factor. DIA set to 10.0 hours.
data_gaps: Unlogged meals prevent isolating baseline static ISF efficacy from dynamic ISF scaling.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are fully enabled and active continuously. Delivering up to 20 minutes of basal equivalent via SMB every 3 minutes manages meals without carb logging, but creates severe insulin stacking during postprandial rises.
data_gaps: No carb entries to evaluate standard SMB with COB versus unannounced UAM microbolusing.

analysis_steps.findings: Critical safety limits are dangerously elevated. Max IOB is set to 25 U while average TDD is only 19.7 U/day (>125% of daily total). Max basal is set to 12 U/h against a peak scheduled basal of 0.8 U/h (15x multiple). Dynamic ISF at 70% drops effective ISF to ~28 mg/dL/U during high readings, causing severe over-dosing.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_iob_units=25 U vs average total daily insulin 19.7 U; max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h vs max profile basal 0.8 U/h; dynamic ISF scaling drops ISF down to 27.8 mg/dL/U at 245 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: 100% reliance on unannounced meals creates a recurring pattern: postprandial glucose rises to peak at 16:00 (avg 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1% TAR), triggering intense reactive SMB delivery that causes a severe crash at 19:00 (avg 105.4 mg/dL, 15.3% TBR).
analysis_steps.evidence: Zero carb entries logged. Hourly local glucose shows 16:00 TAR 32.1% followed by 19:00 TBR 15.3%. Manual correction boluses delivered during UAM (e.g. 1.1 U on Aug 14) compound stacking.
data_gaps: User meal times and carbohydrate amounts are unrecorded.

analysis_steps.findings: Min 5m carb impact is set to 8 mg/dL/5 min. During UAM events, oref1 decays estimated carbs on board rapidly, falsely assuming meal absorption is complete while real absorption persists, triggering secondary SMB microbolus waves.
analysis_steps.evidence: min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min, meal_max_absorption_hours=7.0 h in profile raw settings.
data_gaps: Exact meal composition cannot be determined without user carbohydrate entries.

analysis_steps.findings: Prioritized action plan established: 1) Reduce excessive AAPS safety limits immediately to constrain runaway insulin stacking; 2) Moderated Dynamic ISF aggressiveness from 70% to 50%; 3) Raise overnight target to 100 mg/dL to reduce overnight hypos; 4) Transition to upfront carb logging with prebolusing.
analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesized from stages 1-8 evidence, prioritizing safety constraints before profile or meal adjustments.

strengths: Overall glycaemic control achieves 86.0% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), exceeding the clinical benchmark of >70%.
Average glucose is well-controlled at 121.6 mg/dL with excellent CGM data quality (98.7% coverage).
Automated closed-loop system effectively limits daytime hyperglycemia without requiring manual meal boluses.
issues: Elevated hypoglycemia risk with Time Below Range <70 mg/dL at 5.1% (clinical standard is <4.0%), featuring severe low extremes down to 41 mg/dL.
Concentrated overnight hypoglycemia between 00:00 and 04:00 Local, reaching peak TBR of 18.5% at 01:00.
AAPS Max IOB limit of 25 U exceeds 100% of average Total Daily Dose (19.7 U/day), offering zero protection against insulin stacking.
AAPS Max Basal limit of 12 U/h is 15 times higher than peak scheduled basal (0.8 U/h).
Dynamic ISF adjustment factor at 70% excessively tightens ISF during unannounced meal spikes (down to ~28 mg/dL/U), driving postprandial crashes at 19:00 (15.3% TBR).

recommendations.title: Reduce AAPS Max IOB and Max Basal Safety Limits
recommendations.description: Current Max IOB (25 U) exceeds average daily insulin requirement (19.7 U/day), and Max Basal (12 U/h) is 15x peak basal. Lowering Max IOB to ~7.0 U (~35% TDD) and Max Basal to 3.5 U/h (~4x max basal) provides essential software protection against runaway insulin stacking.

recommendations.title: Moderate Dynamic ISF Adjustment Factor
recommendations.description: Dynamic ISF at 70% overly intensifies insulin delivery during high readings (reducing ISF to ~28 mg/dL/U), directly driving the 15.3% TBR hypo spike at 19:00. Lowering the adjustment factor to 50% moderates microbolus aggressiveness.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target to 100 mg/dL
recommendations.description: The overnight target of 90 mg/dL from 00:00 to 08:00 leaves no safety margin during a window with 10%-18.5% Time Below Range. Raising target to 100 mg/dL creates a vital safety buffer.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight target of 90 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00 provides no buffer against severe overnight hypoglycemia (18.5% TBR at 01:00). Raising the overnight target segment to 100 mg/dL reduces loop aggressiveness during sleep while keeping daytime target structure intact.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose for 3-5 nights to verify reduction in TBR below 04:00 without increasing morning waking glucose above 130 mg/dL.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Update profile target segments at 00:00 and 23:00 from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Withhold basal change until overnight target is raised to 100 mg/dL and AAPS Max IOB limits are constrained, isolating target effects first.

Morning rise (06:00-08:00) is well controlled with minimal hypo risk (1.3%-2.5% TBR). Retain current segment.
Midday profile is confounded by unannounced meals. Maintain basal stability while addressing UAM SMB limits.
Afternoon glucose elevation is meal-driven rather than basal-deficient. Keep basal steady.
Evening lows at 19:00 (15.3% TBR) are driven by stacked afternoon UAM SMBs. Keep basal steady while moderating Dynamic ISF.
Evaluate late evening basal only after automation safety limits and meal bolus strategy adjustments take effect.
Zero carbs logged in telemetry. Withhold CR changes until user begins entering meal carbs.
No meal carb entries recorded in this window. Retain profile baseline.
Unannounced breakfast meals prevent precise empirical CR re-calibration.
Afternoon meals are currently unannounced. Retain CR baseline until meal bolus logging is established.
No logged meals present to evaluate empirical evening CR accuracy.
Static baseline ISF is appropriate; hyper-reactivity stems from Dynamic ISF 70% adjustment factor rather than profile ISF.
Target of 90 mg/dL overnight leaves zero safety margin during window with peak TBR of 18.5% at 01:00. Raising to 100 mg/dL improves safety.
Daytime target of 100 mg/dL provides appropriate balance between glycemic control and safety.
Align late night target with overnight target (100 mg/dL) to prevent loop from driving down glucose prior to sleep.
A 10-hour DIA accurately reflects modern rapid-acting insulin decay tails and prevents premature basal restoration.
SMB and UAM are necessary core features for this setup. Maintain enabled state.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivery pacing is adequate once Max IOB constraints and Dynamic ISF scaling are corrected.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Max IOB of 25 U exceeds 100% TDD (19.7 U/day), and Max Basal of 12 U/h is 15x peak basal. Lowering to 7.0 U Max IOB (~35% TDD) and 3.5 U/h Max Basal stops dangerous SMB stacking.
Dynamic ISF at 70% drops effective ISF to ~28 mg/dL/U during postprandial highs, causing over-dosing and crashes at 19:00 (15.3% TBR). Reducing factor to 50% restores safe responsiveness.
Carb impact settings are standard; retain current values while user meal bolusing is established.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Transition from 100% unannounced meals (UAM) to logging meal carbohydrates with a 10-15 minute prebolus delivering 60%-70% upfront bolus. For unannounced or complex meals, enter estimated carbs as e-carbs spread over 3-4 hours to provide a smooth COB decay buffer.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Announcing carbs upfront prevents rapid glucose velocity spikes that trigger hyper-reactive Dynamic ISF SMB stacking, eliminating the root cause of the 15.3% TBR hypo crash at 19:00.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log meal carbs and bolus times consistently for 3-5 consecutive days in Nightscout.

exceptions.suggestion: Reduce upfront bolus percentage to 50% or set a High Temp Target (110-120 mg/dL) 1 hour prior to eating.
exceptions.rationale: 18:00-20:00 is a window of high hypoglycemia vulnerability (15.3% TBR at 19:00). Lowering upfront insulin protects against overnight stacking.

exceptions.pattern: Postprandial Spikes (>180 mg/dL) during active UAM SMB delivery
exceptions.suggestion: Withhold manual correction boluses if AAPS is actively delivering SMBs.
exceptions.rationale: Manual corrections during active UAM SMB delivery bypass loop IOB constraints and cause severe low extremes down to 41 mg/dL.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Reduce AAPS safety limits in settings: lower Max IOB from 25.0 U to 7.0 U and Max Basal from 12.0 U/h to 3.5 U/h.
Step 2: Adjust Dynamic ISF adjustment factor in AAPS settings from 70% to 50%.
Step 3: Update profile target segments at 00:00 and 23:00 from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL in the active profile.
Step 4: Monitor glucose continuously for 3-5 days, specifically observing overnight TBR (00:00-04:00) and evening stability (18:00-20:00).
Step 5: Begin logging meal carbohydrates in Nightscout with a 10-15 minute prebolus to evaluate empirical Carb Ratios.
education: Max IOB in an automated closed-loop system acts as a hard safety ceiling. Setting Max IOB higher than total daily insulin requirements allows the loop to deliver unlimited microboluses during unannounced meals or sensor noise spikes.

Dynamic ISF increases insulin delivery aggressiveness as glucose rises. While effective at capping high spikes, an overly aggressive adjustment factor can cause severe insulin stacking when insulin action lags behind CGM trends.
Prebolusing 10-15 minutes before meals matches insulin peak action with carbohydrate absorption, flattening postprandial glucose peaks and preventing reactive loop over-dosing.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice or directives.
The user must independently verify every proposed change with their diabetes care team.
Make setting changes one at a time, allowing at least 3-5 days between modifications to evaluate glucose impact safely.
Monitor glucose closely during overnight hours and have fast-acting carbohydrates readily available when adjusting closed-loop settings.
